quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Computer and information research scientists conduct research into fundamental computer and information science as theorists, designers or inventors, and develop solutions to problems in computer hardware and software.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Computer and Information Research Scientists) include Computer Scientist, Research Scientist, Computer Specialist and Scientific Programmer Analyst.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed): most of these occupations require graduate school.

sections.heading: What a computer research scientist does
paragraphs: Computer and information research scientists conduct research into fundamental computer and information science as theorists, designers or inventors, and develop solutions to problems in computer hardware and software.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Computer and Information Research Scientists. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Analyse problems and develop solutions that involve computer hardware and software.
Apply theoretical expertise and innovation to create or apply new technology.
Carry out logical analyses of business, scientific, engineering and other technical problems.
Meet managers, vendors and others to get cooperation and resolve problems.
